both from Cleveland. He was a trumpet player, in charge of the rehearsals and in charge of the band when Echols was in his dressing room and Don Byas was at that time with Eddie Barefield over in the Cotton Club along with Tyree Glenn, and of course when I was at the Cotton Club with Lionel Hampton we had one of the greats, a tenor, Herschel Evans. It was such a joy to hear him blow, he was great. You know, in later years, he gained fame with Count Basie and Lawrence Brown came out of California, too, to join…

I see. What of the Hampton orchestra, do you remember any of the personnel of that band, do you remember who did some of the arrangements for that band? That was before his big break with Benny Goodman.
